measuredFidelity.note: The rig's 6.75-degree leg splay (render.leg-stance) settled ankle daylight at 48.5% against the concept's 46.9%. Round 7 then found that Junebug's SIGNATURE idle pose carried an 8-degree inward leg roll, authored when the rig ran its legs straight down, which closed the ankles to 0.325ft against the bind pose's 0.756 and failed rubric 3.12 in idle while the bind-pose render this command reads stayed correct. The same roll was in all five signature idles and was removed from all of them; an FK sweep now reads every idle within 2% of bind. Re-measured 2026-08-12 after the detector itself was rebuilt to work for the whole roster: the backdrop is now sampled per column (seven sheets are vignetted past the old tolerance), a column counts as occupied by fraction rather than by any single pixel, and the shoe's two tones are read off the concept instead of the hardcoded red/cream that was Junebug's own shoe. Her shoe deltas TIGHTENED, from +2.23/+2.93 under the old classifier to +0.43/-0.78 as tone shares (41.2/25.5 concept against 41.6/24.8 delivered); the round-7 critic note below quotes the old red/cream figures and is left as the record of what was measured then.

frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: The large read is right and it is right by measurement, not by eye: head 34.0% of figure height against the turnaround's 33.9% (+0.10), head width:height 0.82 against 0.84, ankle daylight 48.5 against 46.9. With colour stripped she is still unmistakably the scowling kid with a bun, a headband and a swept tail. Held off 5 by butt-joined primitives, and I re-observed all three the round-7 critic named, each cropped at 4-10x from the region I cite. (1) BUN/CROWN SHELF, junebug-front-review.png x 220-330 y 55-115: the bun sits on the crown ring with a hard vertical step at BOTH silhouette edges and a shadow line across its base — no fillet, a visible corner, dead centre in the front view. (2) HEADBAND STUB, junebug-profile-review.png x 285-370 y 55-165 at 10x over a magenta backdrop: the band's rear end is a flat-cut rectangle terminating in silhouette against true background, where the concept sweeps it behind the ear to the nape. (3) PONYTAIL TIP, x 290-520 y 40-310: the tail tube ends on a flat circular cut and a separate smaller blob is stuck onto it, the seam a full crease ring with a notch either side, against a concept tip that tapers to a drawn arrowhead. A fourth: the pelvis is a flat-bottomed slab that overhangs the thigh tubes with a hard horizontal ledge across the whole hip, visible on the front board at 4x (x 180-360 y 370-420) and on both profile boards. Nothing is severed — a connected-component pass over all four boards returns exactly one component each.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Child proportion is exact and measured, not asserted: head height delta +0.10 points, head aspect -0.02, ankle daylight +1.61 — every 6b metric inside tolerance, and the head:body read is the turnaround's, never the proxy's. The A-pose boards hold the drawn stance with the arms down and daylight between the thighs and calves, so 3.12 passes on the board and again in the run still. The second clause of the 4 bar — 'joints read as connected forms' — is where it stops. The pelvis-to-thigh is the offender: build_leg's top ring simply terminates at 1.72ft inside a separately built seat, so at 4x on both the front and profile boards you see a slab overhanging a narrower tube with a lip, not a hip. The knee is nearly formless too — the ring table runs 0.180 at the knee against 0.172 just above it, a 5% swell that renders as a straight tapering cylinder in profile. It stays a 4 because the joints that carry motion hold: the run still shows a round deltoid under the sleeve cap, a continuous elbow line and a knee that bends without tearing, and the jersey hem covers the pelvis ledge at every gameplay camera.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The one category below the floor, and the deciding clause is the 4 bar's own words: 'one designed mass'. What ships is four stacked primitives with five visible joins. MEASURED first. Default band (5-45% of head height) reads 1.38 minima/row against the concept's 3.82 — 36% of the strand count at 146% of the prominence. That band is not trustworthy on this kid: on both sheets it spans the headband, whose two edges count as FALSE creases, so I re-ran it on a hair-only band. At 2-14% (bun crest and crown, above the band on both sheets) the concept reads 3.00 minima/row and the delivered reads 0.04 — 1% of the concept's strand count. At 2-22%, 1%. At 2-30%, 8%. The bun is a mathematically featureless dome, which the rubric caps at 4 on its own. Then the joins. (a) The bun butt-joins the crown on a hard shelf with a corner at both silhouette edges (front board 10x, x 220-330 y 55-115) and the toon outline pass draws it as a graphic line at gameplay scale in junebug-runtime-hero.png. (b) The hair tie is a FLAT QUAD SLAB, not a wrap: at 10x over magenta it is a single plane crossing in front of the tail whose lower edge is a hard flat cut with true background beneath it, and at gameplay scale in the run still it reads as a yellow tab stuck to the side of the head. (c) True background — alpha 0, sampled at (310,72) and (315,80) of junebug-profile-review.png — shows through the notch between the bun and the ponytail root, so the two masses do not touch; the tail hangs off the head through a narrow neck below the tie. (d) The tip blob. The 4 clauses it does pass are real and worth saying: the hairline is a proper sculpted widow's-peak that reads clean against skin from the front, there is no bare-skull read from any angle, and the headband arch itself is the best-authored accessory on the sheet.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The strongest sculpted category. Garments read as constructed at 5x on the A-pose board: the V-collar is a rounded piping TUBE rather than a painted line, the placket carries three raised button studs, the sleeves have two white stripes plus a real white cuff band, the belt is a band with two loops and a buckle, the knicker gathers into a darker cuff, the sock has its own band, and the shoe has a distinct lighter midsole slab and a red toe cap. The shoe's split is measured, not eyeballed: dominant tone 63.7% of the band against the concept's 64.7, second tone 31.1 against 27.2, mean saturation 34.9 against 36.8. Off 5 on the laces, which are three raised rectangular slabs on the vamp — they do not cross, have no eyelets and no weave, and on the right shoe of the front board one slab breaks the shoe's silhouette (x 160-390 y 590-710 at 4x). Secondary: the jersey hem is a flat horizontal slab cut with square corners rather than a hem that falls over the hip.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The face is a FORM, and I checked the specific things that separate a form from a sticker. A real nose breaks the profile with a defined tip and a nostril underside (junebug-profile-review.png x 210-320 y 110-240 at 8x). No decal-island seam anywhere — I looked for one at 8-10x on both the front and the profile and the atlas wraps the cheek and temple planes continuously. The ears are the best-constructed detail on the whole model: outer helix rim, inner concha shadow, and a lobe sitting against the skull, which settles 3.10 with no ambiguity. Features are legible at hero scale and the angled scowl brows still read at 40px. The chest patch I thought was a texture island at 4x is a specular gradient — resolved at 10x, not a defect. Held off 5 by the mouth. At rest it is a thin flat stroke a few pixels tall, close to the 'collapses to a line' the rubric warns about, and the expression RANGE does not survive: I pixel-diffed a 46x36 mouth box across the four runtime stills and grin/cheer/tongue are the same mouth (grin vs cheer 99 of 4968 channels differ by more than 12, max 39; cheer vs tongue 202, max 70) while only angry is distinct (650-669, max 120). Cropping the source atlas confirms it is the asset, not the capture instrument: cells 1, 10 and 11 are three near-identical open smiles, so the tongue cell has no tongue out and the cheer cell is no wider than the grin. All four stills are genuinely painted — byte sizes 291673/291988/292081/292276, a 0.2% spread, and all four show grass, sky and the character.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Identity survives both ends. At hero (junebug-runtime-hero.png, devstats reads 'model model', so this is the delivered GLB and not proxy evidence) the read is complete: scowl brows, big eyes, white headband arch, dark bun, tail swept to her left. I generated my own 40px read by resizing the front board to 40px tall, and every load-bearing element holds — dark bun over a white band, red top, pink pants, red socks, white shoes, and the angled brows are still two dark marks that say 'determined'. Off 5 on two counts. First, in the FRONT view at field scale the ponytail is entirely hidden behind her, so at 40px she is a bun-and-headband kid and the signature tail — the thing the turnaround draws an arrow at — contributes nothing to the read from the camera the fielder is most often seen from. Second, the tie reads at hero as a flat yellow tab rather than a wrap (junebug-runtime-run.png x 415-595 y 140-290 at 6x), which is a hero-scale accessory defect, not a hair-only one.

Daylight between the ankles 13.0 vs 0.0 is the recorded stance conflict, not a proportion.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: Noodle is bald by design (sculpt-noodle-source.py line 61 'he is bald; brows are atlas ink', line 7 'the first head whose crown is its own skin'), so the designed mass is the dome and measure:strands' 11%/331% is skin-texture noise, not a hair verdict. The dome reads bald from every gameplay angle and the five crown rows did what they were asked: the plateau walk down the crown (x=590, y128-215 on noodle-runtime-hero.png) still shows the same three cel-ramp tones (191 | 159 | 132) that main showed (186 | 157 | 132) — the bands are the toon ramp's steps, not facets — but the step EDGES that were kinked polylines on main are now smooth curves (mean |d2| 2.160 -> 0.886 hero, 2.319 -> 1.023 swing, 1.056 -> 0.880 grin; run 1.000 -> 1.160, noise). What keeps it at 4 and not 5: the rubric caps a smooth featureless mass at 4, and on this kid the featureless mass is the point; the remaining read of three flat diagonal tone bands across the crown at hero is a shader-ramp story on a large uniform surface, not a sculpt defect, and the sheet's dome has one soft highlight with continuous falloff.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: Nothing in the clothing moved this build (git diff main on sculpt-noodle-source.py touches only the crown-row line and a comment), and every clothing finding carries on the current boards: the tee has stripes, a hem and ribbed wrist cuffs; the shoes' two straps are still flat cream stripes on the outer quarter with no throat, eyelets or tongue (noodle-front-review.png 5x x195-345 y555-670); the dark diagonal sliver still crosses the midsole from the tan upper into the cream cupsole on both shoes (14x x216-250 y620-650, a 2px-wide, ~7px-long black-brown wedge ending in a point); the toe and heel tabs are still on the profile; and the TEAM_MASK rolled cuff (judged by extent only — it covers exactly the roll, which is right) is still a smooth cylinder wider than the jean leg above and the shoe below with a hard step at each end and no fold edge (6x x200-340 y555-615). The concept shoe (noodle-turnaround.png x100-320 y700-810) has a laced throat, eyelets and a dark side chevron.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: The mouth latitude is fixed and measured: a local-contrast row scan of noodle-front-review.png (band x250-290, rows darker than the row mean by 30+) puts the smile stroke at rows 210-218 = 75.2-80.1% of the 89-250 head, centred ~77.6-78.3% against the traced 78.9, with eight rows of clear skin (202-209) between it and the rim bottoms at row 201 (69.6%); main's scan put the stroke at rows 202-207 (70.2-73.3%), pressed on the rims. On the four runtime stills the mouths now sit under the rims where the sheet's small smile is: grin shows teeth (noodle-runtime-face-grin.png 4x x430-630 y120-310), cheer is an open mouth with teeth and tongue whose bottom lands ~8px above the chin outline (8x x490-570 y230-290), tongue reaches down to ~5px above the chin outline and stays on the head (8x x490-570 y240-300 — Clover's lesson checked, it fits), angry is a real frown clearly separated from the rims (4x, frown at x320-420 y560-600 of the crop) where main's angry frown sat on the rim bottoms like a moustache. The nose rows landed: at 8x on noodle-front-review.png x220-320 y170-250 there is now a soft lit mound with a faint shadow beneath it between the rims and the smile, and in profile (8x x180-280 y180-280) a rounded nub under the lens where main had a small pointed tab. One named thing short of the drawing: the brows still ride the rim tops at the gameplay camera in all four stills — fat dark arcs whose outer ends clear the rims but whose centres fuse with them; the sheet itself puts the brows one row above the rims (rows 196-202 vs 203), so this is the camera's elevation folding a faithful placement onto the rims, not missing ink. For 5 the nose would need the sheet's two nostrils and a bulb edge (noodle-turnaround.png x180-230 y250-270); it has neither. The visible-face metric is still OFF (-9.79/-8.41, tol 6) and did NOT move — the dome patch is byte-identical to main (rgb(224,201,178), sat 0.21, 4% of pixels pass isSkin) — this is the recorded skin-warmth class from finding 2 and is not filed again.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: The 40px strip on noodle-fidelity-review.png (x940-1010 y545-605) keeps the identity: bald dome, two dark rim dots, cream/blue stripes, blue jeans, tan shoes. The hero read on noodle-runtime-hero.png is now a clean close-up of Noodle: the crown's band edges are smooth curves (measured above), the mouth ink is no longer pressed against the near lens — the only mouth ink visible from the rear 3/4 hero camera is a small dark corner at the jaw edge under the lens (x610-630 y270-285), separated from the rim by skin, which is what a mouth corner looks like from behind the cheek. hairMass.label: hair mass
